claim_1.claim: Flow Cytometry analysis of PBMCs from 63 healthy individuals collected at baseline one week before vaccination (day -7), immediately before vaccination (day 0), and after vaccination on days 1, 7, and 70 showed wide baseline variation in frequencies of many cell populations on day 0, with many B-cell subsets displaying low within-subject variability over more than two months compared to inter-subject variability.

sources.quote: Examination of 126 PBMC subsets (Biancotto et al., 2011) (Figure S1B and Table S2) revealed a wide range of frequencies for many cell populations on day 0 (Figure S2B).

Among populations with high overall variability, many B cell subsets showed low within-subject variability (and therefore high temporal stability) over a period of more than two months (indicated in dark gray in Figure 2A).

claim_2.claim: Flow Cytometry analysis of PBMCs from 63 healthy individuals showed that vaccination on day 0 induced largely non-overlapping cell-subset changes on day 1 and day 7, with day 1 increases in activated innate populations including CD40+ and CD86+ monocytes and IFNa+ plasmacytoid DCs, and day 7 changes primarily in adaptive populations including plasmablasts and activated T-cell populations, compared to day 0 baseline.

sources.quote: As with the transcriptome, changes in subset frequencies on days 1 and 7 were largely non-overlapping (Figure 3D).
Again, day 1 changes reflected activation of innate immune cells, including CD40+ and CD86+ monocytes (ID65 and ID67) and IFNa+ plasmacytoid DCs (ID78)

Day 7 responses primarily reflected changes in adaptive cell populations, including plasmablasts (ID87) as expected, but also a related CD20+ B subset that expressed CD27 and CD38 (ID96, Figure S3), as well as activated T cell populations.

claim_3.claim: Flow Cytometry analysis of PBMCs from subjects clustered by baseline serology and memory B-cell status showed that the more naive group had significantly greater increases in plasmablasts on day 7 after vaccination (day 7) compared to the less naive group.

sources.quote: However, the more naïve group exhibited significantly greater increases in plasmablasts (ID87) and seasonal vaccine-specific ELISpot responses on day 7 (Figure 4C).

claim_4.claim: Flow Cytometry analysis of baseline PBMCs from 63 healthy individuals showed that day 0 cell population frequencies alone were predictive of vaccine response endpoints, with predictive populations for adjMFC including memory, naïve and transitional B cells, CD4 effector memory T cells, IFNa+ myeloid dendritic cells, and several activated T-cell populations.

sources.quote: Notably, predictive models could be built by using cell populations alone (Figure 6B)—integrating pathway/transcript with cell population data performed substantially worse (best median AUC was 0.6 vs. 0.78 using cell populations alone). Thus, day 0 cell frequencies alone provided the essential information for prediction.

Twelve cell populations were identified for adjMFC, including memory, naïve and transitional B cells, CD4 effector memory T cells, IFNa+ myeloid dendritic cells (mDC), and several activated T cell populations (Figure 6C; see Methods).

claim_5.claim: Flow Cytometry analysis of baseline PBMCs showed that most predictive B-cell and some CD4+ T-cell populations were temporally stable within individuals over more than two months, and models trained on day 0 cell-population data accurately predicted adjMFC using independent baseline measurements from day -7 and day 70 compared with the original day 0 baseline.

sources.quote: Except for ID105 (CD86+IgD+ memory B cells), all of the B cell and some of the CD4+ T cell (including effector memory) predictive populations were remarkably stable within individuals over a period of more than two months (Figure 6D).
Highly accurate prediction could still be made for all k's, e.g., AUC=0.91 and AUC=0.86 for days -7 and 70 using k=10, respectively. Thus, the predictive signals were remarkably stable over time.

claim_6.claim: Transcription profiling by array of PBMCs from 63 healthy individuals showed substantial baseline transcript abundance variation on day 0, with subject-to-subject baseline differences contributing substantially to the observed variability of many genes and pathways.

sources.quote: Transcript abundance for day 0 PBMCs also showed substantial variation (Figure 2B), likely reflecting in part the different proportions of cell subsets among subjects.

Assessment of inter- vs. intra-subject variation demonstrated diverse patterns, with subject-to-subject baseline differences (blue bars) contributing substantially to the observed variability of many genes and pathways (Figures 2B and C).

claim_7.claim: Transcription profiling by array of PBMCs from 63 healthy individuals showed coherent but largely non-overlapping post-vaccination gene-expression signatures on day 1 and day 7 after vaccination (days 1 and 7) compared to day 0 baseline, with day 1 enriched for innate immune-cell activation including Interferon-related genes and day 7 enriched for adaptive pathways associated with plasmablasts including ER stress and N-glycan biosynthesis.

sources.quote: As previously reported (Bucasas et al., 2011; Nakaya et al., 2011; Obermoser et al., 2013), we also found coherent changes in gene expression, with largely non-overlapping signatures on days 1 and 7 (Figures 3B and 3C).
Overall, day 1 responses included pathways reflecting innate immune-cell activation, including Interferon-related genes
By day 7, adaptive pathways were more predominant, including those strongly associated with plasmablasts, such as “Endoplasmic Reticulum (ER) stress” and “N-glycan biosynthesis”

claim_8.claim: Transcription profiling by array of PBMCs after vaccination showed that day 1 gene expression was not predictive of antibody response endpoints, although Interferon Signaling correlated robustly with MFC, whereas day 7 transcript data yielded highly predictive models for both adjMFC and MFC.

sources.quote: While models built using either gene expression or cell populations from day 1 were not predictive, “Interferon Signaling” correlated robustly with MFC (Figure 5C).
In contrast, highly predictive models could be built using day 7 data for both adjMFC and MFC (Figures 5D).

claim_9.claim: Transcription profiling by array of baseline PBMCs showed that neither day 0 gene expression nor pathway activity alone was predictive of either vaccine response endpoint, although genes associated with pattern recognition and Interferon signaling robustly correlated with MFC more than with adjMFC.

sources.quote: Neither day 0 gene expression nor pathway activity (defined in Figure S2C) alone was predictive of either endpoint, although a number of robustly correlated genes and pathways could be identified (Figure 6A).
Notably, genes associated with pattern recognition and Interferon signaling robustly correlated to MFC, but less so to adjMFC.

claim_10.claim: Transcription profiling by array of PBMCs showed that transcripts and pathways correlated with predictive cell subsets linked day 7 plasmablast-related populations ID87 and ID96 to antigen-secreting cell genes including Ig chains, XBP1, and IRF4 and to ER stress and N-glycan biosynthesis pathways, compared with their frequencies across subjects.

sources.quote: As expected, the two predictive and coherently changing cell populations from day 7 (ID87 and ID96) were linked to known antigen secreting cell/B cell/plasmablast-specific genes, including Ig chains, XBP1 and IRF4, as well as plasmablast-associated pathways such as ER stress (Figures 7B and D).

These populations were also associated with N-glycan biosynthesis, consistent with the highly glycosylated state of immunoglobulins and the requirement for proper glycosylation for plasma cell development

claim_11.claim: Neutralizing Antibody Titer Assay analysis of serum from 63 healthy individuals showed a wide range of baseline seasonal vaccine titers, while most of the cohort was naïve for pH1N1 based on titers, and subjects with higher initial titers had lower day 70 over day 0 fold-changes after vaccination compared to subjects with lower initial titers.

sources.quote: As expected for subjects from the general population, we found a wide range of baseline titers to the seasonal vaccine
In contrast, most of the cohort was naïve for the pH1N1 virus based on titers
Interestingly, subjects with higher initial titers tended to have lower fold-changes.

claim_12.claim: Neutralizing Antibody Titer Assay analysis of serum from subjects clustered by six baseline serologic and memory B-cell parameters showed that the more naïve group had higher day 70 mean fold-change in titers than the less naïve group, with mean fold-change in titers on day 70 inversely correlated with initial titers.

sources.quote: Thus, both the plasmablast response on day 7 and mean fold-change in titers on day 70 were inversely correlated with initial titers.
Group 1 individuals were generally low for all six parameters, whereas group 2 had mostly higher values

claim_13.claim: ELISpot analysis of PBMCs from 63 healthy individuals showed strong but highly variable increases in influenza vaccine-specific IgG+ antibody secreting cells on day 7 after vaccination (day 7) compared to day 0 baseline.

sources.quote: As expected, we observed strong, but highly variable, increases in influenza vaccine-specific IgG+ antibody secreting cells on day 7 (Figure 3A).

claim_14.claim: ELISpot analysis of PBMCs from subjects clustered by baseline serology and memory B-cell status showed that the more naïve group had significantly greater seasonal vaccine-specific ELISpot responses on day 7 after vaccination (day 7) compared to the less naïve group.

sources.quote: However, the more naïve group exhibited significantly greater increases in plasmablasts (ID87) and seasonal vaccine-specific ELISpot responses on day 7 (Figure 4C).
